attacks.claim: The beta results (0 lost saves, 11 conflict prompts all resolved) are reported as complete for Nov 18-30. Today is 2026-10-26 and the release is Dec 2, so that beta cannot have run yet. The main evidence that saves are safe has no verifiable provenance and may be a plan or projection presented as results.
attacks.evidence: "Nov 18-30: public opt-in beta branch on Steam (2,300 players) and Epic sandbox testers (150). 0 lost saves; 11 conflict prompts, all resolved by players."

attacks.claim: Epic has never been exercised in production. QA and the Epic beta ran on the dev sandbox, and the Steam QA build was on a private branch with no stated tie to the shipping build ID. The 1.3 downgrade was tested only on Steam. Epic is 29% of players and gets the full release at once. The kill switch limits the damage.
attacks.evidence: "Epic build 1.4.0-cl5521 on the Epic dev sandbox"; "Downgrade to 1.3 (Steam beta branch `1.3-legacy`)"

attacks.claim: The overwrite guarantee and the patch-note promise conflict with the auto-download path. Whether the local slot is 'older' depends on cross-device timestamps and an undefined 'since last sync' baseline. A 1.3 round trip may also leave the sidecar stale. Local backups (last 3) limit the loss.
attacks.evidence: "Nothing is overwritten without that choice." vs "downloads the newest cloud copy if the local slot is older"; "Your saves on this PC stay where they are."

attacks.claim: The server keeps only 5 versions per slot with no protection for a known-good copy. Uploads are not validated, so repeated uploads of bad saves could evict good versions. There is also no integrity alert (rejected blobs, fallback events), and the restore alert is anchored to a beta rate from a population about 100x smaller.
attacks.evidence: "the server keeps the last 5 versions per slot"; "any spike in restores > 3× the beta rate"

attacks.claim: The 1.3 downgrade test covers only reading. It does not show that 1.3 preserves the new modifier keys on write-back. The budget-stop kill switch and the atomic one-link-per-account rule are also untested.
attacks.evidence: "Loads, sidecar and modifier keys ignored"; "hard project budget stop at $600/month... flipped automatically" (no QA row)

attacks.claim: The data inventory says 'no name', but sync.meta carries a device name that may contain one. The retention of the steam↔epic link record is also unstated.
attacks.evidence: "device name" vs "No email, name, payment or friends data."; "Cloud data with no sync for 24 months is deleted"

attacks.claim: The load test (30k concurrent launches) is not tied to the patch-day peak or to the first-enable upload. The forecast storage figure does not follow from the stated per-slot limits. Rollback timing for 1.3 on Epic is unspecified.
attacks.evidence: "Load test: 30k concurrent launches syncing in 10 min"; "forecast ~140 GB at 60% opt-in"
